questions.story: A business social media account relies on a single password shared across three marketing team members.
questions.question: What is the safest way to provide team access to a business social media account without compromising primary credentials?
options: Storing the shared password in a central, unencrypted text file on a shared drive
Utilizing official platform team management hubs (e.g., Meta Business Manager) with role-based access control
Sending the login password via SMS whenever a teammate needs to log in
Writing the password on a sticky note attached to the main office computer
questions.feedback: Shared direct passwords eliminate individual accountability and prevent Multi-Factor Authentication from operating securely.

questions.story: A fraudster posing as 'Platform Verification Support' contacts your business on WhatsApp, demanding the 6-digit SMS code sent to your phone.
questions.question: Which security principle protects against social engineering attempts targeting verification tokens?
options: Strict enforcement of a zero-trust policy stating One-Time Passwords (OTPs) and verification codes are strictly confidential and never shared
Sharing the code only if the support agent provides an official-looking badge image
Reading the code out loud over the phone if the caller promises to restore account features
Posting the verification code in a public group chat
questions.feedback: Legitimate platforms and support teams will never ask users to verbally disclose or forward an SMS/app verification code.

questions.story: You suspect an unknown device has gained access to your business account after followers report receiving scam links.
questions.question: What is the most direct method to verify intrusion and identify an unauthorized device's connection details?
options: Changing the account profile picture to see if it changes back
Posting a public story asking if anyone is logged into the account
Auditing the 'Active Sessions / Where You're Logged In' security menu to review connected devices, locations, and session IDs
Deleting and reinstalling the social media mobile app
questions.feedback: Active session management gives complete visibility into active login tokens, enabling immediate manual termination of unrecognized devices.

questions.story: An attacker silently alters primary recovery details on a business social media page to prevent the rightful owner from resetting the password.
questions.question: Which telemetry trigger alerts the primary owner to a high-risk administrative change?
options: Immediate email and SMS alerts sent when primary contact details, recovery phone numbers, or linked email addresses are modified
Checking your bank account balance at the end of the week
Reviewing public engagement metrics on recent posts
questions.feedback: High-security platforms send out-of-band alerts whenever core authentication settings change, giving owners a window to revert unauthorized actions.
